    Guide
    Settings, paces and how the plan works

    Name

    Your running numbers

    Runs are set by distance; the times next to them are estimates at your pace. Without a 5K time the app uses starting paces for a heavier runner coming back from a knee rehab, about 8:00 per kilometre easy. Pace is minutes per kilometre: 8:00 means eight minutes for each kilometre. Add a 5K time when you have one and the paces become yours.

    How the week works

    Seven days, no rest day: four lifting days and three run days. Sunday chest and biceps, Tuesday lats and triceps, Thursday light upper back and chest plus Legs A, Saturday shoulders and arms plus Legs B. Monday, Wednesday and Friday are run days only: knee rehab, then mobility, then the run. The Monday easy run is the recovery day; if the week feels heavy, shorten it or walk it.

    Running heavy, on a cut, after a knee rehab

    About 16 km a week: 4 km easy, 6 km of intervals, 6 km long. Distance is the target, time is only an estimate, so slow is fine. In a calorie deficit your easy pace will be slower than you expect and that is correct: go by effort, not the watch. Eat something with carbs before the interval and long-run days, keep protein high, and don't add runs to burn more, the cut does that on its own. If a run feels flat, slow down rather than skip it. If the knee is warm or swollen the next morning, cut the next run's distance by a third and keep the rehab block.

    Knee rehab

    Eleven months after ACL and meniscus surgery, preparing for football and martial arts. The 17-minute block before every run is general return-to-sport work: quad control, glute strength, single-leg balance, trunk, and small hops forward and sideways. Mobility after it is 13 minutes, so the two together are 30. It is not a medical plan. If your physio gave you exercises, do theirs instead and tell me so I swap them in. Stop anything that gives sharp pain, locking or swelling that lasts to the next day.

    The three run efforts

    Easy
    Zone 2. Full sentences, nose breathing. Slower than feels natural. Most of your running.
    Hard
    The 600 m intervals. A few words at a time. Same pace on every rep.
    Firm
    The long-run finish. Comfortably hard, short sentences, about half-marathon effort.

    Reading a lift

    3 × 8–10 means three sets of eight to ten reps. Pick a weight where the last rep of each set is hard but clean. When you hit the top of the range on every set, go up 2.5–5 kg next time. Tempo like "Down 3 s, up 1 s" tells you how fast to move: slow on the way down, controlled on the way up.

    Running in Kuwait heat

    • Run early morning or after sunset, or use a treadmill at 1% incline.
    • On hot days go by effort, not pace. You'll be slower at the same RPE and that's correct.
    • Carry water with electrolytes on the long run.

    What's from the post and what's added

    Exercises, sets, reps and run structures are exactly as posted. Descriptions, tempo, rest times, warm-ups, equipment, alternatives, pace maths and the timers are added on top as general guidance. Each lift shows a start and finish photo from the public-domain Free Exercise DB, plus a hand-picked YouTube tutorial under Watch form.

    Programme: @wahab.alsaleh on Instagram. Your settings stay on this phone. Gym mode ticks and swaps last for the day only and are never saved.
